summary: The exact instruction text the model receives in production, generated from a markdown source file.
purpose: Keep the model's rules fixed and reviewable in one source file.
why: The header states that the markdown file is the source of truth and a test keeps the two identical.
how: 1) Authors edit the markdown source. 2) This text is generated from it. 3) An injection test compares the two. 4) Callers are expected to pass this text as the system instruction; that use is not visible in this packet.
inputs: None at run time; it is a fixed text constant.
outputs: A single text constant holding the system instructions.
risks: Hand edits here are overwritten or caught by the test. The rules shape model output quality, and the packet cut the text, so the full rule set could not be checked.
debug: If the sync test fails, regenerate from the markdown rather than editing this file. If model output breaks a rule, check the rule in the markdown source.
